question: Rocks which have solidified from molten magma are called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous Rocks**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Igneous Rocks** are formed from the solidification of molten magma.
 
• They are one of the three main types of rocks, along with sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.
 
• Examples of igneous rocks include granite, basalt, and pumice.
 
• These rocks are primarily classified based on their mineral composition and texture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous rocks** can be further classified into intrusive and extrusive types based on where the molten magma solidifies.
 
• Intrusive igneous rocks form below the Earth's surface, while extrusive igneous rocks form at the surface.
 
• The word "igneous" comes from the Latin word "ignis," meaning fire, indicative of their fiery origin.
 
• Igneous rocks play a crucial role in the rock cycle, contributing to the formation of other rock types through weathering and erosion.
 
• They are commonly used in construction due to their durability and strength.
